title: Northlight Health — pilot outbound & technical fit notes
content:
TL;DR: Northlight Health (regional provider network, ~260 clinics, recent EMR migration to CloudMD) is a strong pilot candidate for a 6–8 week evaluation of Redwood Private (VPC) + Optimize to power an internal triage assistant for RN intake and provider note drafting. Primary concerns: PHI handling, uptime/SLOs, and unit economics. Goal: get a 6-week technical pilot on VPC with a narrow scope (RN triage, 2 models endpoints) and a short SOW.

Quick profile:
- Org: Northlight Health (Midwest regional provider network)
- Size: ~260 clinics, 7 hospitals, 4k+ clinicians
- Tech hints: CloudMD EHR (hosted in AWS us-east-2), SAML SSO, Okta identity, internal MDM, internal API gateway (Kong)
- Compliance posture: HIPAA required, BAAs mandatory, SOC2 in progress
- Decision makers: 
  - Dir of Digital Ops: Karen Lee (economic + pilot signoff)
  - Head of Clinical Ops: Dr. Samuel Ortiz (clinical safety / adoption)
  - Cloud Platform Lead: Ankit Sharma (networking, VPC, KMS)
  - Procurement: Lisa Nguyen (procurement/legal chatter)
- Champion: conversation with RN lead (Marta Reyes) is positive — cares about time-saved for triage and fewer admin tasks

Why Redwood fits (initial hypothesis):
- Private deployment + customer-managed VPC meets PHI/KMS requirements (BAA + HSM/KMS integration is required to close deal)
- Dedicated capacity option for predictable throughput during clinic peak hours (08:00–11:30, 14:00–17:00 local)
- Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) to control token costs for high-volume RN intake workflows
- Rollout tools for staged clinical validation (canary on test clinics -> prod clinics)

Suggested pilot scope (6 weeks):
1) Two endpoints only: Intake triage chat (internal RN tool) + note-draft generator (provider-facing draft)
2) Data flow: EHR snippets (de-identified where possible) -> internal staging bucket -> Redwood Private VPC endpoint (no PHI persisted unless encrypted/approved)
3) Success metrics: p95 latency < 350ms for short prompts, 95% triage suggestions clinically sensible (qualitative), average cost < $0.015 per completed interaction (ballpark)
4) Deliverables: config + infra runbook, KMS/HSM integration plan, acceptance test checklist, pilot retrospective with topline ROI

Outbound / email sequence (working drafts):
- Subject ideas: "Pilot: Triaging RN Intake with Private LLMs (6-week)" / "Low-risk triage pilot for Northlight — private deployment"
- Opening line (cold): "Hi Karen — quick note: we helped a regional provider reduce RN intake time by ~28% using a private LLM deployed into their VPC. Would you be open to exploring a short pilot to validate safety and throughput?"
- Mid-sequence CTA: "If a 6-week VPC pilot with a scoped SOW sounds reasonable, I can send a one-pager with technical safeguards (BAA, KMS, audit logs)."

Call script bullet points (discovery focus):
- Confirm EHR / data flow and ability to send de-identified snippets
- Ask: "Who owns KMS/HSM and how do they prefer integration — native AWS KMS, external HSM?"
- Clarify usage pattern: concurrent sessions per clinic, expected prompts/day, sensitive PHI types allowed
- Risk/questions: audit trails for model outputs, retention, deletion policy

Topline objections and rebuttals (prep):
- Objection: "We can’t send PHI to a third party."
  - Rebuttal: "We propose Redwood Private with a customer-managed VPC; all traffic stays inside your VPC and we support integrating with your AWS KMS or HSM. We'll sign a BAA and provide full audit logs—legal + security will have an explicit SAML/Okta flow."
- Objection: "Model hallucinations risk clinical safety."
  - Rebuttal: "Pilot scope excludes autonomous recommendations — outputs are labeled as drafts for clinician review; we’ll configure model profiles and guardrails, and run evals on your prompts to measure regression. Canary rollout to a small clinic first."
- Objection: "Cost — ongoing token spend is unpredictable."
  - Rebuttal: "Dedicated capacity + Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization, batching, prefix caching) gives predictable unit economics; we can provide cost sims for your estimated traffic and propose a capped pilot spend."
- Objection: "Vendor lock-in concerns."
  - Rebuttal: "Redwood supports model version pinning and clear export paths for KV caches and configs; the API abstraction lets you switch underlying models if needed."

Technical notes / things to validate with Cloud Platform Lead (Ankit):
- VPC peering vs PrivateLink preferences, expected egress/inbound rules
- KMS: customer-managed (preferred) — needs key rotation policy compatibility
- Network throughput: pilot estimated peak concurrency ~180 sessions across clinics -> need Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom
- SSO: Okta SAML integration for admin console logins and RBAC
- Logging/observability: must ship logs to their Splunk/Datadog and maintain 90-day audit retention

Initial sizing and ballpark economics (very rough):
- Estimate: 5–7k triage prompts/day over pilot; average tokens per interaction 400 tokens
- If using a mid-tier open model with quantization: estimated effective cost ~ $0.01–$0.03 per completed interaction (after batching/kv cache)
- Suggest prepaid pilot credit cap $10k for 6 weeks to cover experimentation and infra config

Risk register (things legal/security will dig into):
- BAA process timeline (usually 2–4 weeks)
- Penetration test / attestation requirements for VPC package
- Data residency (must remain in us-east-2)
- Model evaluation for clinical safety (need clinician review subset)

Next actions (my todo list):
- [ ] Draft one-pager for Karen with pilot scope + safeguards (due 2026-02-16)
- [ ] Align with Ankit on VPC connectivity options (schedule techcall, target 2026-02-19)
- [ ] Loop in Security (Priya) to prep BAA + SOC2 artifacts request
- [ ] Build very short demo flows (mock RN intake -> draft note) for live demo
- [ ] Prepare cost sims and a capped pilot pricing sheet

Meeting notes from 2026-02-10 exploratory call with Marta (RN lead):
- Marta: current pain points — back-and-forth with providers after intake, ~9 minutes avg triage per patient
- Wants: triage suggestions to reduce repeat clarifying Qs, ability to copy into EHR without extra steps
- Concern: speed during peaks and offline fallback if inference fails
- She’s open to 6-week pilot if clinicians have final signoff and audit trail is clear

Warm intro templates (for internal use):
- To Eng: "Ankit — Karen encouraged a quick tech sync to validate VPC options. We propose 30m to review KMS choices and network setup. Can we do Wed/Thu next week?"
- To Security: "Priya — starting a BAA conversation for Northlight pilot; will share spec + expected data flows. Appreciate a quick scan and list of required attestations."

Misc brain dump / experimentation ideas (not for legal):
- Try a tiny local evaluation harness with 500 de-identified notes to test hallucination rates and build a confusion matrix for common triage intents
- Consider a hybrid workflow: embeddings + vector DB inside VPC for retrieval + smaller LLM for generation to reduce token usage
- Track adoption metrics: suggestions accepted, time-saved per intake, clinician satisfaction (NPS-ish)

Notes to self:
- Keep outreach human and clinical-focused; avoid generic ML buzzwords in initial threads (focus on safety, workflow, ROI)
- Expect procurement to ask for a pilot SOW and a line-item for BAAs and pen tests
- Follow up cadence: 3 business days after email, then 7, then attempt intro via mutual connection (Marta knows a vendor that used similar tech)

End of scratchpad.

(If this looks promising, convert to a one-pager and attach the short demo flow screenshots.)
